findings.evidence: No hit for `starCartanMatrix_transpose`/`chainEntry_comm` anywhere in TauCeti (grep). Mathlib states exactly these for its simply-laced Cartan matrices: `mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Cartan.lean:160` `@[simp] theorem A_transpose : (A n).transpose = A n` and `:163` `theorem A_isSymm`.
findings.fix: Add `lemma chainEntry_comm (s t : ℕ) : chainEntry s t = chainEntry t s` and `@[simp] lemma starCartanMatrix_transpose : (starCartanMatrix ℓ).transpose = starCartanMatrix ℓ` (plus `starCartanMatrix_isSymm`).
findings.issue: `starCartanMatrix` is documented as "simply laced by construction" and `chainEntry` as depending only on the difference of positions, but no lemma states symmetry. A consumer needing `starCartanMatrix ℓ v w = starCartanMatrix ℓ w v` (to check the generalized-Cartan-matrix axioms of an embedded star, or to apply `IsFiniteType.transpose` from Basic.lean) must redo the case analysis over `chainEntry`.

findings.evidence: Line 104 `@[simp] lemma chainEntry_succ_succ (s t : ℕ) : chainEntry (s + 1) (t + 1) = chainEntry s t`; line 136 RHS `chainEntry ((v.2 : ℕ) + 1) ((w.2 : ℕ) + 1)` matches that LHS.
findings.fix: Drop `@[simp]` from `chainEntry_succ_succ` (the file's own use at line 240 is an explicit `simp only [chainEntry_succ_succ]`, so nothing breaks), or restate `starCartanMatrix_some_some` with `chainEntry (v.2 : ℕ) (w.2 : ℕ)` on the right.
findings.issue: `@[simp] starCartanMatrix_some_some` has RHS `if v.1 = w.1 then chainEntry (↑v.2 + 1) (↑w.2 + 1) else 0`, which the simp lemma `chainEntry_succ_succ` (line 104) rewrites on the spot. The simp-normal form of a same-arm entry is therefore `if v.1 = w.1 then chainEntry ↑v.2 ↑w.2 else 0`, a form no stated lemma exhibits.

findings.evidence: grep for `starMark_none_eq` across TauCeti returns only its declaration (line 167) and two in-file uses (lines 281, 356).
findings.issue: `starMark_none_eq` is a public product-rearrangement step (a specialization of `Finset.mul_prod_erase`) used only inside this file's two row computations; it is proof machinery, not part of the star API.

summary: The star matrix is advertised as simply laced but exposes no symmetry lemma, and one entry simp lemma is stated in a form simp immediately rewrites away; one proof-internal helper is public.
